 Monaco’s form stalls in Ligue 1 as Filipe Luis chases a response at Paris FC 
 Go to the comments section Add to your bookmarks Share this article Early-season pacesetters Monaco have stalled over three Ligue 1 matches and now need a response against Paris FC on Sunday at 17:15 at Stade Jean-Bouin. For Filipe Luis, who has enjoyed a smooth start since his appointment, it feels like a first real imperative.
 According to Le Progres, a perfect Conference League run contrasts with domestic slips, with draws against Toulouse, 2-2, and Lille, 1-1, at home, then a 1-0 loss at Lorient, where a blunt attack proved costly.
 OneFootball Videos
 Luis maintains his side have largely matched opponents but lacked control of the outcome because of inconsistency. Each time they missed a half, the second against Toulouse and the first against Lille, and paid for it.
 Aleksandr Golovin puts the wobble down mainly to bad luck and says greater efficiency is needed in the box. Monaco average 12.9 shots per game, eighth in Ligue 1, with 4.6 on target, eleventh. He has three league assists but no goal and accepts he must do better.
 Senior figures have wavered too. Captain Denis Zakaria was replaced on 51 minutes against Toulouse and on 66 at Lorient, then withdrawn at the break against Lille. Luis values him but says he was not offering exactly what the team needed at those moments.
 Eric Dier’s injury kept him out at Lorient and against Lille, and his return is keenly awaited. Luis considers the Englishman fundamental to on‑field organisation, including as captain on set pieces.
 Roles are shifting after two months, with Folarin Balogun, Mika Biereth, Takumi Minamino, Mohammed Salisu, Christian Mawissa and Matthis Abline short of minutes, while Paris Brunner, Edan Diop and Sadibou Sané emerge. Luis accepts there is plenty to fix and highlights the second-half intensity against Lille as a template, while staying hard to play.
 Source: Le Progres
